name: Wumeng Yi
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Retired Glottolog languoid merged into Wusa Yi [ywu] in 2008; only ISO change-request documentation exists

sources.citation: Gerner, Matthias. 2019. Highlights from three Language Families in Southwest China: Burmese-Lolo, Tai-Kadai, Miao. RFLR Monographs 3. Duisburg: Research Foundation Language and Religion. Sec. 1.3.1 Phonology (Weining Neasu), pp. 4-6.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent: consonants (11 retroflexes), vowels, four contrastive tones 55/33/21/13, syllable C(C)V(V)T; a full-text search for stress/accent/'accent' returns nothing. Describes the Yi of Weining county, which Glottolog files under Wumeng Nasu [wume1235].

sources.citation: Lama, Ziwo Qiu-Fuyuan. 2012. Subgrouping of Nisoic (Yi) Languages. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Arlington. Nesu (Weining) profile pp. 76-77.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent. p.76-77: 'The Nesu includes varieties Wusa Nesu [nɯ55su33] (Weining County of Guizhou), Wumeng, Mangbu, Shuixi Nesu.. The Nesu has 46 initials, 8 vowels.., 4 tones (/55/, /33/, /21/, and /13/) (cf. YYFC 1983).' No stress/accent statement anywhere for Nesu.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-037 (submitted by Jamin R. Pelkey with David Bradley): retire [ywm] Yi, Wumeng and merge into [ywu] Yi, Wusa; adopted 2008-01-14. 8 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; denotation/identity only. Rationale (p.2): 'Wumeng and Wusa have long been recognized as distinct varieties of Nasu, but Wumeng is spoken primarily in Guizhou Province with some speakers also living in Yunnan Province.. [ywm] should be merged into [ywu]'. Only source cited: Bradley 2007, Atlas of the World's Languages 2nd ed.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 pages for wume1235 (Wumeng Nasu), wume1236 (Wumeng Yi, bookkeeping), nesu1235 (Nesu); Wikipedia 'Nasu language' (en); 彝语东部方言 (zh).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Glottolog lists only Wu 2020 (phonology) and Gerner 2002 (specific feature) for wume1235 and nothing for wume1236; zh-wiki gives a Wuding phonology (4 tones) and places 乌蒙土语 in Zhaotong/Yongshan.

sources.note: Snippet only (no page opened): '贵州威宁彝语有 55、33、13、21 四个声调。其中 13 调多用来拼写汉语借词。彝语有些音节,除有声调而外,还带表意重音或表情重音。重音一般是靠强化句中某词(或词素)原有的重读音节来表示的。这种重读音节较一般音节略长。凉山彝语叹词和摹写自然声响的象声词,都带表情重音..' -- Weining Yi tones, then a general-Yi remark on semantic/expressive stress illustrated from Liangshan (Northern) Yi; no rule for where word stress falls in Wumeng/Weining Yi.
